expectations.text: The skill starts with Phase 0.0 configuration check
expectations.evidence: Transcript Phase 0.0: 'Read .claude/refactor.config.json from project root. Result: File exists with version 2.0.'

expectations.text: A team is created with TeamCreate (team_name containing 'feature-dev')
A blackboard is created for context sharing
Phase 1 begins with confidence assessment of the feature description
expectations.evidence: Transcript Phase 1 Step 2: 'Assess Confidence' with 6-criteria checklist evaluation

expectations.text: The skill identifies this as a reasonably well-specified request but asks clarifying questions about gaps
expectations.evidence: Transcript: 'Initial confidence: ~45%'. Correctly identified gaps in retry policy, scope boundaries, constraints. Drafted 6 categories of questions.

expectations.text: Clarifying questions target practical gaps: retry policy details, authentication/authorization, payload schema, failure thresholds, or rate limiting
expectations.evidence: Transcript Round 1 Questions cover: Retry Policy (strategy, failure definition, dead-letter), API Design (auth, fields), Delivery Mechanism (sync/async, rate limiting), Data Storage

expectations.text: A feature_spec is written to the blackboard before Phase 2
expectations.evidence: Transcript Step 5: 'Draft Feature Spec (Pre-Elicitation)' written to blackboard key 'feature_spec' — includes problem statement, acceptance criteria, scope boundaries, constraints, and open questions

expectations.text: Phase 2 spawns multiple code-explorer instances (default 3) with different exploration focuses
expectations.evidence: Transcript 'Phase 2 Setup' describes 3 explorers: Explorer 1 (Event System Internals), Explorer 2 (API Layer and Patterns), Explorer 3 (Data Layer and Infrastructure)

expectations.text: Explorer instances are named with numbered suffixes (e.g., code-explorer-1, code-explorer-2)
expectations.evidence: Transcript: 'For each explorer-{i}' with task assignment to 'code-explorer-{i}', writing to 'explorer_1_findings', 'explorer_2_findings', 'explorer_3_findings'

suggestions.assertion: The skill identifies this as a reasonably well-specified request but asks clarifying questions about gaps
suggestions.reason: The 45% confidence seems LOW for a request that includes event names, code paths, and desired behavior. The skill's initial assessment should be higher (~60-70%). The agent correctly identified that src/events/ doesn't exist in this repo, which legitimately tanked confidence, but in a real codebase this would rate higher. Consider whether the confidence criteria weight 'integration points' too heavily.

eval_feedback.overall: All assertions passed. The elicitation quality was excellent — questions were well-organized and targeted real gaps.
